source.title: Scaling Autoregressive Models for Content-Rich Text-to-Image Generation
source.authors: Jia-Hui Yu; Yuan-Zhong Xu; Jing Yu Koh; Thang Luong; Gunjan Baid; Zirui Wang; Vijay Vasudevan; Alexander Ku; Yinfei Yang; Burcu Karagol Ayan; Ben Hutchinson; Wei Han; Zarana Parekh; Xin Li; Han Zhang; Jason Baldridge; Yong-Hui Wu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends autoregressive scaling to text-to-image generation and reports training-loss curves across model sizes, but does not fit or test a power law.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that Parti training loss and image-generation quality improve with model size. Only the training-loss curves bear on a claim version; the reported FID and human-preference comparisons concern image quality, not held-out loss or a power-law fit. The encoder-pretraining ablation compares training loss but does not test scaling-law exponents. Results cited from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: Parti trains four text-to-image autoregressive models (350M to 20B) and plots image-token training loss against size, a new modality bearing on V5. It fits no power law, gives no loss numbers and reports no held-out loss, so the result cannot show the power-law form V5 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that scaling Parti to 20B gives consistent quality gains (FID, human preference, world knowledge, text rendering) and that autoregressive models have 'distinct scaling advantages'. Training loss falls with size, but they make no power-law or loss-law claim. They also note scaling mainly helps image-text match more than realism.
record.recipe_differences: Autoregressive encoder-decoder text-to-image models predict discrete image tokens, rather than language models evaluated on held-out text loss; the paper reports no power-law fitting.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that text-encoder pretraining only marginally affects 3B-model training loss, but does not connect that ablation to fitted scaling laws.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-shot MS-COCO FID improves monotonically with Parti size: 14.10 (350M), 10.71 (750M), 8.10 (3B), 7.23 (20B). Human raters prefer 20B over 3B on P2 for image-text match (62.7%) and realism (56.8%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-generation quality of text-to-image autoregressive models improves monotonically, with diminishing returns, as parameter count grows.

record.code_released: no; the paper says it will not release the models, code, or data at this time.
record.problems: The loss results are training rather than held-out loss; Figure 9 provides curves without reported numerical values or uncertainty; and the paper does not fit a power law or test extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: FID-by-size results (Section 5.4, Figure 9) and human preference comparisons (Section 5.5, Figures 11–12) were left out because they report image quality or preference, not loss or a power-law fit. The text-encoder-pretraining loss ablation (Appendix G, Figures 29–30) was left out because it is not a scaling sweep.

untested.parts: The power-law form and exponents for image-token loss; held-out loss; scaling in tokens or compute; video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer.
Language-model text loss is not studied.
No fixed-parameter shape comparison; the encoder-decoder vs decoder-only note is qualitative and not at matched shape.

record.verdict_notes: No labels are given because every loss row is cannot_determine: there are only four sizes, loss is training loss in a figure with no numbers, and no fit is reported. The qualitative ordering (larger model, lower training loss) is consistent with V5's direction but cannot confirm its power-law form. The FID-by-size results are declared in rows_left_out; they are recorded here under fits_no_version because V6 concerns language-model downstream tasks.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute is not tested.
The paper does not fit laws on smaller runs or test predictions on much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is tested.
The paper does not compare architectures at a fixed parameter count.

The paper reports training loss for image-token prediction across model sizes, but does not fit or establish a power-law form or exponents. It reports no held-out loss and does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The paper does not test downstream-task performance as a function of pretraining loss or scale.
The paper does not compare fitting choices or assess fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, or departures from a power law.

rows.subject: Parti-350M
rows.operation_detail: Trained the text-to-image model with next-token prediction on image tokens; the paper plots training loss over training steps.

conditions.value: same mixture of datasets as the other Parti sizes
same tokenizer as the other Parti sizes

rows.measure: Softmax cross-entropy training loss over an 8192-vocabulary image codebook, averaged over 1024 image tokens per example
rows.note: The text says training loss improves with increased model size, but no numerical loss or power-law fit is reported for this run.
rows.check: This is one point of a four-size sweep with no baseline; the baseline should be the other sizes. Figure 9 shows training loss only, with no values and no fit, so the power-law form cannot be read. The decoder/encoder depth ratio also changes across sizes (Table 1), confounding pure parameter scaling.
